title: The Painted Skin
lines: A young scholar named Wang encountered a beautiful woman on the road, weeping. She claimed to have run away from a cruel husband. Wang, moved by pity and desire, brought her home and hid her in his study.
For days, Wang neglected his wife and his studies, spending every moment with this mysterious woman. But one morning, he rose early and peeked through the crack in the study door.

What he saw froze his blood. The beautiful woman lifted her face — her real face — off her body and laid it flat on the table, taking up a brush to paint the delicate features of a human countenance onto its blank surface. Underneath was a demon with green skin and a mouth full of fangs.

The scholar fled to a Daoist priest who gave him a fly-whisk to hang at his door. But the demon was not deterred. It tore out Wang's heart and devoured it, leaving his body to be discovered by his faithful wife.

The story ends with Wang's wife begging a mad beggar to bring her husband back to life. The beggar spat phlegm into her mouth and ordered her to swallow it. Disgusted, she obeyed — and later coughed up Wang's heart, which fell back into his chest and began to beat.
Moral: Beauty may be only a painted skin. True virtue lies beneath.
